premises.text: Shared database for applications lets any app add any information to any object
premises.evidence_span: It's a shared database for applications

premises.text: Storing related app data in one place enables queries that combine independent databases
premises.evidence_span: That kind of operation, where I'm combining data from two different databases, is very difficult in the normal world. But when the information is in the same place, it becomes trivial

premises.text: Applications need not know each other or ask permission to contribute data
premises.evidence_span: those applications are not aware of each other. They have no knowledge of each other

premises.text: Platform covers everything from barcodes to people as writable objects for the web of things
premises.evidence_span: FluidDB gives you a shared, writable object for everything. In other words, it's a platform for the web of things

premises.text: Final word on data should not rest solely in the hands of applications
premises.evidence_span: a future where our data, the final word on our data, is not in the hands of applications

domains.name: Web-of-things universal objects and data ownership

value.text: A writable social future of data where related information lives together and is more useful
value.evidence_span: The future of data is a writable future

causal_links.evidence_span: add information to anything without asking for permission
platform for the web of things

notes: Split universal object scope / ownership thesis from core shared-DB query mechanism as separately revisable. Demo mashups not separately premised (§4.1.2).
